The Bangladesh Jute Corporation, in brief, the Corporation on 23-11-99 first presented FMA No. 92 of 2000 against order dated 28-7-99 passed by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 at Dhaka in Title Suit No. 205 of 99 which decreed the suit ex-parte and made the award dated 11-1-95 Rule of the Court. Then, the appellant on payment of ad-valorem court fees got the appeal registered as FA No. 356 of 03 purportedly under section 17 of the Arbitration Act, 1940, in brief, the Act. 

 7. The Corporation appeared and opposed the application by filing a written objection. Learned Subordinate Judge however, ex-parte decreed the suit and made the award of Taka 37,99,583.64 Rule of the Court by impugned judgment and decree dated 28-7-99. Hence, the previous appeal. 

 13. Learned subordinate Judge disposed of both suits by judgment and decree dated 16-7-2001 in decreeing Title Suit No. 136 of 1996 and dismissing Title Suit No. 130 of 1996 and making the award a Rule of the Court. 

 14. Against said judgments and decrees the Corporation presented above First Appeal No. 528 of 2001 and No. 529 of 2001. 

 38. When the Court is satisfied on such requirements and after the time for objection to an award passed and/or the objection, if any filed, is rejected, it shall proceed to pronounce judgment in accordance with the award and upon the judgment so pronounced a decree shall follow. After fulfilling such duty, Court signs a decree, which could only be challenged on the limited ground that whether the decree is in excess of the award or not otherwise in accordance with the award. 

 42. For foregoing reasons, the impugned judgments and decrees making the awards Rule of the Court cannot be sustained in law. The appeals, therefore, succeed.
